nodes.label: Sustainable diet & mind

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Nutrition and food security|Sustainable diet & mind_qna_000
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What were the top factors mentioned by participants when discussing sustainable food consumption habits?
nodes.answer: Participants mentioned factors related to eating British produce, locally sourced food, making conscious food choices considering production and environmental impact, reducing food waste, and eating seasonal produce.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Nutrition and food security|Sustainable diet & mind_qna_001
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How do physical opportunities like moving away from the family home and having control over cooking influence sustainable food consumption habits?
nodes.answer: Physical opportunities like moving away from the family home and having control over cooking can act as enablers to sustainable food consumption habits by allowing individuals to make conscious choices about what they eat and cook. This autonomy can lead to healthier and more sustainable food choices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Nutrition and food security|Sustainable diet & mind_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What negative emotions were evoked in sustainably minded participants when discussing food consumption and climate change?
nodes.answer: Feelings of guilt, pressure, and exhaustion were mentioned.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Nutrition and food security|Sustainable diet & mind_qna_003
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do negative emotions such as guilt and frustration impact consumers' efforts to eat sustainably when substituting out a particular food source?
nodes.answer: Negative emotions like guilt and frustration can deter consumers from engaging with sustainable food behaviours and lead to mental exhaustion regarding food choices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Nutrition and food security|Sustainable diet & mind_qna_004
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are some alternative emotional motivations for consuming sustainable products, according to Yang et al. (2020)?
nodes.answer: Consuming sustainable products can elicit positive emotions and less guilt.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Nutrition and food security|Sustainable diet & mind_qna_005
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Why is taste considered a crucial factor when choosing sustainable food?
nodes.answer: Taste is considered a crucial factor when choosing sustainable food because it provides immediate gratification to consumers, who tend to focus on the present rather than the future benefits of sustainable food options.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Nutrition and food security|Sustainable diet & mind_qna_006
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How do health claims for sustainable food products differ from immediate gratification in consumer preferences?
nodes.answer: Health claims for sustainable food products offer long-term future benefits to consumers, while consumers generally value immediate returns in the form of taste and sensory experience when making food choices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Nutrition and food security|Sustainable diet & mind_qna_007
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Why are health aspects important in sustainable food choices?
nodes.answer: Health aspects are crucial as diets can bridge the gap between environmental sustainability and human health.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Nutrition and food security|Sustainable diet & mind_qna_008
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How do nature sounds impact consumer willingness to buy sustainable food?
nodes.answer: Nature sounds have been found to positively influence connectedness to nature, mood, and willingness to buy sustainable food, as demonstrated in retail field experiments.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Nutrition and food security|Sustainable diet & mind_qna_009
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What are some benefits of being more connected to nature?
nodes.answer: Being more connected to nature promotes pro-ecological behavior and contributes to individuals' health, well-being, and happiness.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Nutrition and food security|Sustainable diet & mind_qna_010
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What is the impact of higher UPF consumption on environmental sustainability?
nodes.answer: Diets with higher shares of Ups had lower environmental impacts, indicating that higher UPF consumption may be more environmentally sustainable.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Nutrition and food security|Sustainable diet & mind_qna_011
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are some key points of synergy between healthy and sustainable eating habits?
nodes.answer: Points of synergy between healthy and sustainable eating habits include reducing meat consumption, increasing plant-based food intake, and avoiding chemicals or processed products. Leveraging these synergies could aid in promoting more sustainable consumption patterns.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Nutrition and food security|Sustainable diet & mind_qna_012
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How did Ernst off et al. (2019) find vegetarian meals to compare with traditional meat meals in terms of environmental impact?
nodes.answer: Ernst off et al. (2019) found that vegetarian meals consistently showed a reduction of environmental consequences of 40 percent in aspects such as carbon footprint, resource consumption, water use, ecosystem quality, and health effects of pollutants when compared to traditional meat-containing meals.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Nutrition and food security|Sustainable diet & mind_qna_013
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does the low level of processing in the Mediterranean Diet contributes to its sustainability?
nodes.answer: The low level of processing in the Mediterranean Diet, consisting mainly of fresh products, contributes to its sustainability by reducing environmental impact.
